tales.title: ქეთევან დედოფალი — Queen Ketevan the Martyr

beats.narration: Far from Kakheti, in Shiraz, Queen ქეთევან is held a hostage at the court of Shah Abbas — a sovereign of Georgia kept as a captive of empire. Witness a queen who has already lost her kingdom's freedom and holds, still, the one thing they cannot take without her consent.

The demand comes: renounce her faith and convert, and live in honour; refuse, and die in torment. This is not a quarrel between peoples or faiths — it is coercion, the Unremembering's bluntest tool, the attempt to make a soul erase itself. Witness her refuse, without hatred and without fear.

In 1624 they torture Ketevan to death for that refusal. You cannot save her; that is the truth of the tale, and her choice is hers. Ward her witness — stand so that her death is remembered as the sovereign act of conscience it was, not erased into one more cruelty of a hard age. The foe is the coercion, never a people.

Her relics are carried home, and Kakheti keeps her as a saint and a queen who would not be unmade. Restore her memory — the proof that a captive with no army and no crown left still held a power no empire could seize: the refusal to forget who she was. The tyranny killed the woman and lost the memory.

Queen Ketevan stands in the Chronicle among the homeland's bravest — a martyr whose courage outshone the throne she had lost. You have kept her. The thread holds, even out of the heart of exile and empire.
